name: Aden (1937–1963)
description: A British Blue Ensign — dark blue with the Union Flag in the canton — charged in the fly with a white disc bearing a two-masted Arab dhow under sail on light-blue water.
history: Adopted in 1937, when Aden was detached from British India and made a Crown Colony. The dhow badge was drawn by George Kruger Gray of the Royal Mint, who treated the vessel heraldically rather than naturalistically; the dhow itself flies the red flag with a white stripe typical of the South Arabian coastal ports. The flag was used until 18 January 1963, when the colony became the State of Aden within the Federation of South Arabia, though it is reported to have remained in use afterwards at Perim and in the Kuria Muria Islands. The surrounding Aden Protectorate, a patchwork of treaty states, had no flag of its own. ADN is the alpha-3 code element indeterminately reserved for Aden under the UN road-traffic conventions.
